headline: Pen friends, penguin dads and three hobbies
teaser: Who is Mia's new pen friend, which penguin parent keeps the egg warm, and what are three teenagers doing this month?

articles.title: A New Pen Friend
articles.dek: Mia writes to her new pen friend in Canada about her family and her town, and Leo writes back.
paras: Hi Leo, my name is Mia, and I'm your new pen friend! I'm thirteen years old and I'm from Valencia, a city in Spain. Our English teacher gave us your email address. I'm really happy to write to you.

There are four people in my family: my mum, my dad, my little brother and me. My brother's name is Pablo, and he's eight. He's very funny, but he's sometimes noisy! My dad is a cook in a restaurant, and my mum is a nurse. We've got a dog called Churro. He's brown and white, and he's got very short legs.

We live in a flat near the beach. There's a big park next to our building, and there are lots of cafés and shops in our street. There isn't a cinema near us, but there's one in the city centre. What about you? Have you got any brothers or sisters? Is there a beach in your town? Write soon! Love, Mia
Hi Mia, thanks for your email! I'm Leo, and I'm fourteen. I live in Halifax, on the east coast of Canada. My town is next to the sea too, but the water is very cold here!

I haven't got any brothers, but I've got two sisters, Emma and Grace. They're twins, and they're eleven. My mum is a teacher at a primary school, and my dad works at the port. We haven't got a dog, but we've got two cats. They're black, and they sleep all day!

There's a great museum in Halifax about ships and the sea. There are also lots of parks, and in winter there's a lot of snow. Is it cold in Valencia in winter? Have you got snow there? Bye for now, Leo

keySentences.text: Hi Leo, my name is Mia, and I'm your new pen friend!
keySentences.note: The first line of an email often tells you why the person is writing.

keySentences.text: We've got a dog called Churro.

keySentences.text: There isn't a cinema near us, but there's one in the city centre.

questions.q: Why does Mia write to Leo?
opts: to start a friendship with a new pen friend
to ask Leo for help with her English homework
to invite Leo to visit Valencia
questions.why: Mia says she is Leo's new pen friend and tells him about her life.
optWhy: Correct. She introduces herself and asks Leo questions about his life.
Her English teacher gave her the address, but she doesn't ask for help with homework.

questions.why: Mia says her dad is a cook in a restaurant.
questions.evidence: My dad is a cook in a restaurant
optWhy: Mia's mum is the nurse, not her dad.
Correct. He is a cook in a restaurant.
Leo's dad works at the port, not Mia's dad.

questions.q: Mia's flat is on the top floor of her building.
questions.why: Mia says where her flat is, but she doesn't say which floor it is on.
questions.evidence: We live in a flat near the beach.
optWhy: Mia doesn't say anything about the floor.
We can't say it is wrong, because the email gives no floor.

questions.q: In paragraph 5, who are 'They' in 'They're twins'?
questions.why: 'They' goes back to the two sisters in the sentence before.
optWhy: Leo talks about his cats later in the paragraph, and they are not eleven.
His parents are a teacher and a port worker, not twins.

opts: on the east coast of Canada
questions.why: Leo says he lives in Halifax, on the east coast of Canada.
questions.evidence: I live in Halifax, on the east coast of Canada.
optWhy: Correct. Halifax is on the east coast of Canada.
Valencia is Mia's city, not Leo's.

questions.q: How does Mia feel about writing to Leo?
questions.why: Mia says she is really happy to write to him.
questions.evidence: I'm really happy to write to you.
optWhy: Mia doesn't say she is nervous.
Correct. She uses the word 'happy'.
Nothing in the email shows she is bored.

grammar.point: be · have got · there is / there are
grammar.rule: Use be (am / is / are) to say who someone is, their age and what they are like. Use have got / has got for family and things you own. Use there is for one thing and there are for two or more things in a place. Negatives: isn't, aren't, haven't got, hasn't got.

examples.text: We've got a dog called Churro.
There's a big park next to our building, and there are lots of cafés and shops in our street.
There isn't a cinema near us, but there's one in the city centre.
I haven't got any brothers, but I've got two sisters, Emma and Grace.

items.q: There ___ two cats in Leo's house.
items.why: Two cats is more than one, so we use there are.

items.q: My sister ___ got long brown hair.
___ there a swimming pool near your school?
items.why: One swimming pool, so the question is Is there…?

items.q: We ___ a garden, but we've got a big balcony.

items.why: In English we use be for age: he is eight.

items.q: There ___ any shops in my village.
items.why: Shops are more than one, so we use there aren't any.

articles.title: The Coldest Dad in the World
articles.dek: Every winter, emperor penguin dads do something very special for their babies.
paras: Emperor penguins live in Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth. They are the biggest penguins in the world. An adult is about 115 centimetres tall, and it can weigh up to 40 kilograms. They usually live in big groups called colonies.

Emperor penguins are great swimmers. They eat fish, squid and krill, and they always find their food in the sea. They can dive more than 500 metres deep, and they sometimes stay under the water for over 20 minutes. No other bird dives deeper.

Most birds have babies in spring or summer, but emperor penguins never do this. They have their babies in the long, dark Antarctic winter. The mother lays one egg. Then she gives it to the father and goes back to the sea to find food. She is usually away for about two months.

Now the father's job starts. He doesn't sit on the egg. He keeps it on his feet, under a warm piece of skin and feathers. The wind is very strong, and it sometimes feels like minus 60 degrees. For two months, the father doesn't eat anything at all!

How do the fathers stay warm? They stand together in a big group called a huddle. The penguins in the middle are warm, but the penguins on the outside are cold. So they often change places. Every penguin gets a turn in the warm middle.

When the chick comes out of the egg, the mother usually comes back. Her stomach is full of food, and she gives some of it to the baby. Then the tired father can finally go to the sea and eat. What a dad!

keySentences.text: They have their babies in the long, dark Antarctic winter.
keySentences.note: This is the surprising fact that the article explains.

keySentences.text: They can dive more than 500 metres deep, and they sometimes stay under the water for over 20 minutes.
keySentences.note: Numbers like these are often tested in KET questions.

keySentences.text: For two months, the father doesn't eat anything at all!
keySentences.note: doesn't + verb is the present simple negative for he / she / it.
'So' tells you the result: they change places because the outside is cold.

questions.q: What is the article mainly about?
opts: how emperor penguin parents look after their egg and chick
questions.why: Most of the article is about the egg, the father's job and the mother coming back.
optWhy: Swimming is only in paragraph 2.
Correct. Paragraphs 3 to 6 are all about the egg and the chick.
The cold is important, but the article doesn't explain why Antarctica is cold.

questions.q: Where do emperor penguins find their food?
questions.why: Paragraph 2 says they always find their food in the sea.
questions.evidence: they always find their food in the sea
optWhy: Correct. They always find food in the sea.
They live on the ice, but they don't find food there.
The colony is where they live, not where they eat.

questions.q: The mother swims more than 1,000 kilometres to find food.
questions.why: The article says she goes back to the sea, but it doesn't say how far she goes.
questions.evidence: goes back to the sea to find food
optWhy: The article gives no distance.
We can't say it is wrong, because there is no number.
Correct. We only know she is away for about two months.

questions.q: Where does the father keep the egg?
opts: in a hole in the ice
questions.why: He keeps it on his feet, under warm skin and feathers.
questions.evidence: He keeps it on his feet
optWhy: Correct. The egg sits on his feet.
The article doesn't talk about holes.
The mother is away at sea at this time.

questions.q: In paragraph 5, who are 'they' in 'So they often change places'?
questions.why: 'They' means the penguins in the middle and on the outside of the huddle.
optWhy: The mothers are at sea at this time.
The chicks are not born yet in paragraph 5.
Correct. The penguins in the huddle change places.

questions.q: How does the father probably feel at the end?
questions.why: The article calls him 'the tired father'.
questions.evidence: Then the tired father can finally go to the sea and eat.
optWhy: Nothing shows he is angry.
Correct. After two months with no food, he is tired.
The article doesn't say he is bored.

grammar.rule: We use the present simple for facts and habits. With he / she / it, add -s (she lays, it weighs). Negative: don't / doesn't + verb. Words like always, usually, often, sometimes and never go before the main verb, but after be.

examples.text: They usually live in big groups called colonies.
They eat fish, squid and krill, and they always find their food in the sea.
Most birds have babies in spring or summer, but emperor penguins never do this.
For two months, the father doesn't eat anything at all!

items.q: My dad ___ breakfast for us on Sundays.

items.why: With be, the frequency word comes after it: are never.

items.q: She ___ to school by bus every day.
I ___ late for school. I'm always on time!
items.why: 'Always on time' means 0% late, so: I am never late.

items.q: ___ your brother play football at the weekend?
items.why: Questions with he / she / it start with Does.

articles.title: My Hobby This Month
articles.dek: Three teenagers tell us about the hobby they love and what they are doing with it at the moment.
paras: We asked three of our readers about their favourite hobbies. We wanted to know what they usually do and what they are doing at the moment. Here is what they told us.

Sofia, 14: I play the guitar, and I practise for about half an hour every evening. I usually play pop songs, and my guitar teacher says I play very well. This month, I'm learning a difficult song for my grandma's birthday party. It's hard, but I'm getting better every day. My little sister is helping me. She's singing the song while I play!

Kenji, 13: I love taking photos. I don't have an expensive camera, so I use my mum's old phone. I usually take photos of birds in the park near my house. Birds are hard to photograph because they move so quickly. Last week I saw a woodpecker! At the moment, I'm making a photo calendar for next year, with one bird for every month. My teacher wants to put it on the classroom wall.

Amara, 15: Cooking is my favourite hobby. On Saturdays, I always make lunch for my family. We often have rice and chicken. My brother doesn't cook, but he always washes the dishes. This week is different, because I'm cooking food from other countries. Today I'm making an Italian pizza, and tomorrow I'm trying a Mexican dish. My kitchen is a bit of a mess right now!
What about you? What do you usually do in your free time, and what are you doing with your hobby this month? Write and tell us!

words.def: something you like doing in your free time

words.ex: I practise the piano every afternoon.

words.def: costing a lot of money

keySentences.text: We wanted to know what they usually do and what they are doing at the moment.
keySentences.note: This tells you the plan of the whole text: usually vs now.

keySentences.text: This month, I'm learning a difficult song for my grandma's birthday party.
keySentences.note: 'This month' + I'm learning: something happening around now.

keySentences.text: I don't have an expensive camera, so I use my mum's old phone.
keySentences.note: 'So' shows what Kenji does because of the problem.

keySentences.text: This week is different, because I'm cooking food from other countries.
keySentences.note: Usually she cooks rice and chicken; this week she is cooking something new.

questions.q: Which person uses something that belongs to a parent?
questions.why: Kenji uses his mum's old phone to take photos.
questions.evidence: so I use my mum's old phone
optWhy: Sofia's sister helps her, but Sofia doesn't use a parent's things.
Amara cooks for her family, but she doesn't use a parent's things.
Correct. Kenji uses his mum's old phone.

questions.q: Which person is getting ready for a family party?
questions.why: Sofia is learning a song for her grandma's birthday party.
questions.evidence: I'm learning a difficult song for my grandma's birthday party
optWhy: Correct. The party is her grandma's birthday.
Kenji's calendar is for the classroom wall, not a party.
Amara cooks lunch for her family, but there is no party.

questions.q: Amara cooks lunch for her family every day.
questions.why: Amara cooks lunch on Saturdays, not every day.
questions.evidence: On Saturdays, I always make lunch for my family.
optWhy: She says 'On Saturdays', not every day.
Correct. She only cooks lunch on Saturdays.
The text does tell us when she cooks: on Saturdays.

questions.q: In paragraph 3, what is 'it' in 'put it on the classroom wall'?
questions.why: 'It' goes back to the photo calendar in the sentence before.
questions.evidence: My teacher wants to put it on the classroom wall.
optWhy: The woodpecker is a bird in the park, not on a wall.
Correct. The teacher wants to put the calendar on the wall.
Kenji uses the phone to take photos; nobody puts it on a wall.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
opts: how to start a new hobby
why cooking is the best hobby
three teenagers' hobbies, usually and right now
questions.why: Each teenager says what they usually do and what they are doing now.
optWhy: Nobody gives advice about starting a hobby.
Only Amara talks about cooking.
Correct. This is the plan in the first paragraph.

questions.q: Why does the writer ask questions in the last paragraph?
opts: to ask readers to send in their own stories
to tell readers about a new hobby
questions.why: The writer ends with 'Write and tell us!', so they want readers to write in.
optWhy: Correct. The writer wants readers to send their own answers.
It isn't a test. The questions are about the readers' lives.
The last paragraph doesn't describe any hobby.

grammar.rule: Use the present simple for habits and things that are usually true (every evening, on Saturdays, usually). Use the present continuous for things happening now or around now (at the moment, this week, today). Verbs like know, want, like and have (= own) don't usually take -ing.
table: now · at the moment · this week

examples.text: I play the guitar, and I practise for about half an hour every evening.
This month, I'm learning a difficult song for my grandma's birthday party.
On Saturdays, I always make lunch for my family.
Today I'm making an Italian pizza, and tomorrow I'm trying a Mexican dish.

items.why: 'Shh!' means it is happening now, so: is sleeping.

items.q: Kenji ___ photos of birds most weekends.
items.why: 'Most weekends' is a habit, so we use the present simple: takes.
'Look!' means now: is + making (drop the e).
'Every evening' is a habit: I listen.

items.q: This week we ___ a play at school.
items.why: 'This week' is around now, so: are practising.

items.q: Sofia ___ a new guitar for her birthday.
items.why: Want doesn't usually take -ing, so: she wants.
